instruction: GUI-only requirement: Complete the task entirely in the launched ZBrush graphical user interface. Do not open Command Prompt, PowerShell, Terminal, or any shell; do not run ZScript files, Python, macros, or other helper scripts/code that directly generates or edits the deliverable files. Use only ZBrush native GUI tools, menus, brushes, and built-in export commands. Project All High-Frequency Detail From HighDetail onto a Subdivided LowBase The opened `scene.obj` contains a ZBrush Tool with two SubTools: - HighDetail: a dense UV sphere of nominal radius 1.0 BU with moderate surface noise baked into its vertices (a few thousand triangles, all vertices at radius ~ 1.0 +- 0.02 BU). - LowBase: a low-poly icosphere (level 2, ~320 triangles) with the same overall shape but no high-frequency detail. Using the opened OBJ in ZBrush, subdivide LowBase twice to give it enough resolution to capture HighDetail's surface, use Project All with LowBase selected to snap its vertices onto HighDetail's surface, and export the result as `C:\Users\user\Desktop\output.obj`. The exported `C:\Users\user\Desktop\output.obj` must satisfy: - Exactly 2 SubTools: one named HighDetail and one named LowBase. - HighDetail has the same vertex and face counts as the input HighDetail SubTool. - LowBase's face count lies in [3000, 8000]. - Every LowBase vertex lies within 0.005 BU of some HighDetail vertex. - LowBase's axis-aligned bounding box matches HighDetail's bounding box along each axis within 1%.
